# Kelly museum expansion — 27 October 2026

The catalogue now contains **259 records**, **158 SVG studies**, and **101 explicit pending study slots**. This pass adds 66 primary museum painting rows and 49 source-reviewed SVG studies. Reconciliation of four pre-existing duplicate identities makes the net catalogue increase 36 records from the previous 223; records are not a certified count of the oeuvre.

SFMOMA’s full 154-object public artist listing was classified:31 paintings,29 drawings,19 collages,12 prints,54 photographs,8 sculptures,1 artist’s book. Their source references remain available; a misleading geometric substitute was not created.

Its public open-access archive excludes the Kelly works and cannot establish zero holdings or completeness. ## Additional collections

Glenstone’s 82 artist-index links were fetched/classified within this project’s painting/support scope, yielding 11 painting rows and 8 new SVGs. Two existing SVGs remain; Yellow Curve stays pending because the Foundation and museum report different floor footprints and the reference is an oblique installation view.

Fort Worth’s exact creator facet has 6 objects:5 paintings imported and 1 serigraph excluded. All 5 paintings now have SVGs. Nelson-Atkins’s 8 artist records have 1 painting,6 photographs and 1 lithograph; its painting White Black now has a source-reviewed SVG. All 285 objects across these seven public indexes were reviewed, with Hirshhorn’s partial coverage recorded separately. A public index is not a guarantee of unlisted holdings.

## Identity and metadata safeguards

Four existing duplicate identities were reconciled after direct image comparison: Gaza, Red Green, Met Black White(1970), and Self-Portrait / Self-Portrait with Thorn. Original source rows, historical title/date/medium/dimension variants and old-to-current record aliases are retained. Met’s bibliography explicitly cites the MoMA 1973 illustration, strengthening that identity match. Same titles alone do not establish identity: SFMOMA’s two 1962 Red White paintings remain separate, as does Foundation EK 290.

SFMOMA’s Spectrum Colors Arranged by Chance was independently compared cell-by-cell with the Foundation EK 63 photograph;1441/1444 black-versus-colour cell decisions agree, with the three threshold differences confined to matching dark-blue cells. Its 1951–1953 museum date range includes the Foundation’s 1953 date.

Per-panel measurements are never substituted for a whole installation. Blue Green Black Red has known individual panels but variable overall width, retained as null. Red-Orange’s conflicting published axis order is flagged. These and schematic wall/floor projections are omitted from true-scale display with explicit counts; they remain in comparable-size mode.

## SVG and interface checks

All 49 new SVGs were authored after actual reference inspection, parsed, rendered and compared with sources. White paint remains opaque; genuine gaps between supports remain transparent. Colours and contours are interpretive. No photographic pixels, scripts or external resources are embedded in the SVGs.

All 322 structured source rows are represented exactly once. Twenty-five automated catalogue/asset checks pass, with separate source and visual audits. Browser verification covered 27 SFMOMASVGs in comparable mode,25 at true scale, four counted missing slots, the two scale exclusions, detail opening and actual recolouring/reset. Collection and all-version filters persist in shareable URLs.

The wider 200-museum search still means 120 artist-mention leads and 80 unresolved searches, not 120 painting holdings. Work-level source records are now incorporated for 37 targets. The remaining queue and catalogue gaps remain explicit.

The authority gap is unchanged: the complete Bois volume inventories have not been accessed or reconciled. This remains a working research catalogue.
